chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about a man who had sheep and cows, and he was aware of the slaughtered from these, so he isolated it, and isolated the dead. Then the dead and the slaughtered got mixed up. So how should he deal with it?' So he said: 'He should sell it to the one who considers the dead as permissible (to eat), and he can eat from its price, for there is no problem with it'.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when slaughtered and dead livestock are mixed and cannot be distinguished?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the practical issue of indistinguishable mixing (ikhtilat) between slaughtered livestock and carcasses. He prescribes selling the mixed group to 'those who eat the dead' (ahl al-maytah), a term Shia scholars often interpret as Jews or Christians, thereby transferring the impurity to them while allowing the Muslim owner to retain the monetary value. This solution highlights the Shia juristic principle that the price of an impure item becomes pure, facilitating economic utility without requiring the owner to bear the loss of the carcass's value.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having been asked about a man who had sheep and cows, and he was aware of the slaughtered from these, so he isolated it, and isolated the dead. Then the dead and the slaughtered got mixed up. So how should he deal with it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should sell it to the one who considers the dead as permissible (to eat), and he can eat from its price, for there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked

about the case of a man who had sheep and cows and he separated the clean and the dead then they became mixed and about what he should do. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can sell it to one who considers dead animals lawful then use what he receives as payment; it is not unlawful.’”
